analysis.title: Global Energy Weekly: Carbon, coal, and conflict
key_insights: The Iran war, which began with the US attack on Feb 28, has caused an energy supply shock. Oil is up about 40% since then, TTF gas is about 2.5x its pre-war level, and NWE ULSD is about 90% higher. Global energy prices are at their highest since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Markets are skeptical of a US-Iran deal by year end (Kalshi odds deteriorating). BofA says elevated energy prices could persist into 2027.
European coal is just under €25/MWh against gas near €90/MWh. Even with the carbon cost added, coal is about half the price of gas, which favors gas-to-coal switching.
Coal switching is capped by capacity. Germany retired nearly 20GW of coal capacity from 2014 to now, and the EU cut about 60GW, roughly 40%.

EU coal generation has risen as gas prices rose. In January coal generation was flat YoY while gas was nearly 12TWh higher YoY. By May both showed YoY gains, with coal's gain larger than gas's, and the gap widened in June. BofA expects data after June to show coal outpacing gas further.

Rising coal generation lifts EU power-sector emissions, which raises EUA demand. From roughly €0 to €80/MT, EUAs rise about €4/MT per €1/MWh increase in gas's premium to coal. Beyond that, coal capacity limits the response.
A 1% rise in industrial emissions in the top five emitting countries is estimated to raise EUAs by about €2/MT.

BofA expects EUAs could reach up to €100/MT this winter on gas-to-coal switching, a cold winter and seasonal strength. It expects EUAs to fall back below €80/MT by 2H27, assuming Middle East LNG exports normalize and new US LNG projects start.
CBAM is now in its operational phase. Importers must buy and surrender certificates priced off quarterly EUA auctions, and free allowances are being phased out. This should tighten the EUA market.

The Commission delayed the EU methane rule on oil and gas imports from Jan 2027 to 2028, with a compliance deadline of May 31, 2029 for 2028 imports. The rule faces pressure for further delay as the EU prioritizes energy security.

ETS2 (road transport and buildings fuels) is scheduled to start auctions in 2027 but faces calls for delay. BofA is bearish on ETS2 because high fuel prices cut driving, and expects EU ETS2a futures could fall from about €75.
Road emissions in France look to be down about 5% YoY so far this year, against a 0.5% annual growth rate over the past ten years.
European retail fuel prices are very high. Euro Super 95 with taxes averages €2.01/liter (up nearly 20% from €1.64 pre-war), and retail diesel is up about 40% since the war began.
US retail gasoline is $4.30/gal and diesel $6.32/gal, with diesel 71% higher since end-February. BofA sees a possibility that kilometers driven per vehicle fall in 2026.

EV adoption is accelerating. Japan's June EV sales were up 187% YoY and India's up 121%. China e-truck sales rose about 80% YoY in Q1, on pace for a third of Chinese truck sales, and are cutting China diesel demand about 10% this year per Bloomberg.

The US responded to high prices with an early winter-blend fuel waiver and a rollback of CAFE standards to 34.9mpg by 2031 from the Biden-era 50mpg. Neither lowered retail gasoline prices, and BofA expects fleet fuel economy to rise regardless.

sector_views.rationale: EUAs get near-term support from gas-to-coal switching, with a possible rise to €100/MT this winter. High energy prices and demand destruction are longer-term bearish.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA forecast. WTI is forecast at $87/bbl.
Prices are expected to ease as the conflict resolves and new LNG supply arrives.
A strong El Niño and LNG constraints should keep coal supported.

macro_indicators.reading: up to €100/MT this winter, below €80/MT by 2H27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Near-term upside from coal switching, longer-term downside from demand destruction and the end of the conflict.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.4mn b/d deficit in 3Q26, 1.5mn b/d surplus by 4Q27
macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA's projected swing from deficit to surplus.
Diesel outlook remains bullish until Hormuz flows normalize.
BofA thinks they could fall from here on weaker road-fuel demand.

risk_factors: Escalation or prolonged war could push energy prices higher into 2027
Low EU gas stocks and a cold winter could lift TTF further
Further delays to ETS2 or the methane rule would weaken the carbon policy tightening
Slowing European manufacturing, partly from rising electricity costs, would cut industrial emissions and EUA demand
Resolution of the conflict and new LNG supply would lower gas prices, move generation back to gas and cut power emissions

tension_points.bull_case: Gas-to-coal switching raises power emissions, a cold winter and seasonal strength add upside, and CBAM tightens supply. BofA sees EUAs up to €100/MT this winter.
tension_points.bear_case: High energy prices destroy demand, EVs cut road emissions, and weaker manufacturing cuts industrial emissions. Conflict resolution would return generation to gas, so EUAs fall below €80/Mt by 2H27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Conflict resolution with Middle East LNG exports normalizing and new US LNG projects starting would end the near-term upside.

theme_stances.key_argument: Gas-to-coal switching and CBAM could push EUAs to €100/MT this winter before demand destruction pulls them below €80/Mt by 2H27.
theme_stances.evidence: EUAs could trade up to €100/MT this winter

theme_stances.key_argument: High fuel prices and EV adoption weaken road emissions, which lowers ETS2 demand and prices.
